config.description: Distilled student on dozken's architecture at hidden 128 -- 225,922 params, 51.8% of his 435,943-param teacher, against v022's 73.8%. Same teacher, same loss, same schedule; the student size is the only change. Also the latency-safe size: v022 at 46.83 us/row already projects to 83% of the time budget, and this should roughly halve that.
config.hypothesis: The distillation gain is COMPRESSION-DEPENDENT, and both data points say so. v017 was 61% of its teacher and landed 0.001880 ABOVE it. v022 is 74% of its teacher and landed 0.004940 BELOW it. More compression means more distillation regularisation, so a more compressed student should land closer to the teacher's 0.690168 -- or above it. If the hypothesis holds, v023 beats v022 while being materially cheaper to serve. If it fails, compression is not the axis and the remaining 0.0049 has to come from the teacher's training recipe instead.
config.change_vs_parent: hidden 160 -> 128 only (321,602 -> 225,922 params). Everything else identical to v022.

train_time_metrics.aggregation: mean of two target-wise global clipped Weighted Pearson correlations over all masked rows

gate score measured on 5 validation sequences -- NOT the official full-validation number
score_interpretation: full_valid_wp 0.684681, trained on cache/train alone so this is clean. -0.000547 against v022's 0.685228, which is -1.7 sigma and INSIDE the 0.000317 noise floor. The compression hypothesis is therefore REFUTED in the form tested: a student at 51.8% of its teacher (225,922 vs 435,943 params) scores the SAME as one at 73.8%, not better. That is a null result on score but a useful one on cost: 30% fewer parameters for 0.0005, and latency 40.12 us/row -> ~42 min on the grader, which is the SAFELY shippable size. If a submission slot must be spent, v023 is the entry to use when runtime headroom matters more than the last 0.0005. Not a promotion candidate: v022 remains our best.
promotion_verdict: Not a promotion candidate. v022 remains the best model at 0.685228 local / 0.6565 public. This run is packaged and documented as a null result on the axis it tested.
latency_verdict: Passes the retired-then-replaced latency gate. Note the grader has now returned actual times for v021 (55m32s, 93%) and v022 (50m46s, 85%), both of which our old 75% margin wrongly rejected, so a projection in the 85% band is known to complete.
